tier_rationale: A purely mechanical keyed padlock: laminated steel body, hardened boron-alloy shackle, non-rekeyable 4-pin cylinder. No battery, electronics, Bluetooth, or app of any kind. Master Lock's own grantee code (MZR) has 36 FCC filings for its radio-equipped products, including a Bluetooth-enabled lock (MZRD1000) and multiple Zigbee/Z-Wave smart locks — confirming Master Lock demonstrably files grants when a product has a radio — and no filing exists under that grantee for the Model 5, satisfying the sibling-control test for a meaningful absence.
the_unplug_test: Nothing to unplug. A key turns a mechanical cylinder that throws dual ball-bearing locking dogs into the shackle. It works identically whether the internet exists or not, whether Master Lock exists or not, and whether the last decade happened or not — the same lock body has been sold for years with no firmware to update and no account to create.

repairability.notes: Body is a sealed laminated-steel stack, not designed to be opened for repair; not rekeyable by design. Shackle and lock are sold as a sealed unit — the product is durable rather than repairable.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: confirms purely mechanical keyed padlock with no electronics/Bluetooth/app; 2in laminated-steel body, 3/8in hardened boron-alloy shackle, non-rekeyable 4-pin W1 cylinder, dual ball-bearing locking, list price $21.47.

Sibling-control check: Master Lock Company LLC (grantee code MZR) holds 36 FCC filings for radio-equipped products, including a Bluetooth-enabled lock (MZRD1000) and multiple Zigbee/Z-Wave smart lock modules, establishing that Master Lock demonstrably files when it ships a radio. A separate targeted search under the same grantee for a 'Model 5' padlock returned no matching filing.

open_questions: Exact current retail price varies by retailer and by keying option (keyed alike vs. keyed different); band reflects the manufacturer's own list price.
No independent teardown was found confirming the sealed body contains no electronic component; relying on the manufacturer's own description plus the FCC absence check.
notes: Recorded as the keyed-padlock answer for the security domain, deliberately contrasted with Master Lock's own Bluetooth padlock line (found via the same grantee search) — the connected version is a sibling product from the identical manufacturer, on the identical shelf.
